subject: Performance SLOs: p95/p99 targets (hosted API vs current provider) - Post-call recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLOs: p95/p99 targets (hosted API vs current provider) - Post-call recap

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + follow-ups from our discovery focused on performance and SLOs so we can scope a meaningful proof-of-concept. Please correct anything I missed.

What we heard from Finlytics (summary):
- Target workload: single-turn text generation for search re-ranking and small summarization tasks. Typical prompt -> 128–256 tokens output.
- Desired end-to-end latency targets (user-facing): p95 <= 200 ms, p99 <= 450 ms.
- Throughput/scale needs: sustained 150 req/s per region, with bursts to 250 req/s.
- Concurrency: ~50 concurrent requests at peak.
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required for UX; first-byte streaming latency ideally <= 120 ms.
- Current provider: you mentioned variability at the tail and some throttling during spikes.

What we need from you to validate/qualify:
1) Baseline numbers from your current provider (p50/p95/p99 end-to-end for the same prompt set, and any observed degradation under sustained load).
2) Sample latency distribution or raw samples (CSV is ideal) so our SREs can compare distributions rather than just aggregates.
3) Any networking constraints (e.g., are clients in EC2 in us-west-2 with expected 30–60 ms network RTT to the provider?)
4) A small canonical prompt set (5–10 representative prompts) and typical token counts so we can run like-for-like tests.

Our proposed next steps:
- I'll put together a synthetic load test plan that mirrors your traffic shape (burstiness, concurrency) and share it by EOD Wednesday.
- If you can share the baseline CSV + the canonical prompt set and a test account/API key (or a short-term test token), our performance team can run a side-by-side using Redwood Hosted API.
- Schedule a 45-minute deep-dive with our SE (Dylan) to review results and tuning knobs (quantization, batching, streaming config) — how does Thursday 10:00–10:45 AM PT look?

Notes on what Redwood typically shows for similar workloads (so expectations are set):
- Hosted API with streaming enabled often reaches p95 in the ~120–220 ms range for 128-token outputs depending on model and region; p99 depends on burstiness and KV-cache hit rates.
- We optimize for tail with request routing, adaptive batching, and prefix caching; we’ll be explicit about the network RTT assumptions when we run tests.

Attachments: none from us yet — we’ll send the test plan and a sample config.

Thanks,
--
Marissa Cole

From: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finlytics Technical Ops <ops@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs: p95/p99 targets (hosted API vs current provider) - Post-call recap

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers and I've attached a short CSV and our Q1 SLA extract for context.

Baseline (CurrentProvider) for the same prompt set we discussed (median token output ~140):
- p50: ~110 ms
- p95: ~350 ms
- p99: ~720 ms
- Sustained throughput we currently provision is ~120 req/s; we see throttling when bursts exceed ~180 req/s.
- Concurrency: typically up to 40 concurrent connections during peak.
- Streaming: supported via websocket; initial first-byte latency usually ~200 ms, then steady stream.

Notes: the p99 tail often correlates with cache-miss scenarios and occasional noisy neighbors on the provider side. Our infra team is including a brief note on observed network RTTs in the CSV.

I've attached:
- SLA_report_Q1.pdf (summary from our procurement team)
- latency_samples.csv (raw end-to-end samples, header: timestamp,region,req_id,latency_ms)

We can also share a short read-only test account for side-by-side trials — I can send credentials to a secure channel if that helps.

Alex
Alex Thompson
Head of Integrations
Finlytics
alex.thompson@finlytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs: p95/p99 targets (hosted API vs current provider) - Post-call recap

Alex — appreciate the files, that helps a lot. Quick follow-ups before our SE deep-dive:

1) Streaming detail: can you confirm typical chunk sizes and whether you use server-sent-events or websockets for payloads? For planning our streaming latency expectations, token chunking (e.g., 32 tokens per chunk vs 128) makes a difference on first-byte and inter-token spacing.

2) Test credentials: yes — a short-lived API key would be ideal. If you prefer a dropbox/secure share, we can accept an expiring GCS/Drive link.

3) Network RTT: if you can confirm the typical RTT from your clients (or from your app-hosting region) to CurrentProvider, we’ll subtract that when comparing end-to-end numbers so we isolate provider vs network contributions.

Proposed schedule: Dylan and I are available Thu, 5 Mar 2026, 10:00–10:45 AM PT for the SE deep-dive. I’ll send a calendar invite now. Agenda: test plan review, baseline comparison, tuning levers (batching/quantization), and success criteria for POC.

I’ll also attach our synthetic-load plan and a short list of the exact prompts we’ll use — sending that in a follow-up within an hour.

Thanks — looking forward to running the tests.

Best,
--
Marissa Cole
